glosses: to haunt (of spirits, thoughts, or people)

To bother, harass, or annoy persistently.

examples.text: He pestered me with questions.
She pestered him to help her.

glosses: To crowd together thickly.

examples.text: That which eſpecialleſt nouriſht the moſt prime pleaſure in me, was after a ſtorme when they were driuen inſwarmes, and lay close peſtred together as thicke as they could packe; the next day following, if it were faire, they would cloud the whole skie with canuas, by ſpreading their drabled ſailes in the full clue abroad a drying, and make a brauer ſhew with them, then ſo many banners and ſtreamers diſplayed againſt the Sunne on a mountaine top.

glosses: A bother or nuisance.

examples.text: By now I presumed I had become a real pester.

glosses: jemanden in übelwollender Absicht oder belästigend aufsuchen

examples.text: In der Nacht wird sie von Geistern und Dämonen heimgesucht.
Die Villa wurde schon zwei Mal von Einbrechern heimgesucht.
Meine Rächer werden euch heimsuchen und zur Verantwortung ziehen.

glosses: als Unglück eintreffen, jemandem zustoßen

examples.text: Und wieder hat eine Seuche das ohnehin geplagte Land heimgesucht.
[COVID-19-Pandemie:] „In Südkorea konnte man […] auf Epidemie-Erfahrung zurückgreifen: In den vergangenen Jahren hatten die Infektionskrankheiten Sars und Mers das Land heimgesucht.“
[Afghanistan] „wird immer wieder von schweren Erdbeben heimgesucht, insbesondere in der Hindukusch-Bergkette. Dort treffen die indische und die eurasische tektonische Platte aufeinander.“

glosses: To inhabit or to visit frequently (most often used in reference to ghosts).

examples.text: A couple of ghosts haunt the old, burnt-down house.
You wrong me Sir,thus ſtill to haunt my houſe.
Foul spirits haunt my resting place.
those cares that haunt the court and town

glosses: To make uneasy, restless.

examples.text: The memory of his past failures haunted him.
The murder of Déagol haunted Gollum, and he had made up a defence.

glosses: To stalk; to follow.

examples.text: The policeman haunted him, following him everywhere.
Ex's and the oh-oh-oh's, they haunt me / Like ghosts, they want me / To make 'em a-a-all / They won't let go / Ex's and oh's

glosses: To live habitually; to stay, to remain.

examples.text: Ieſus therfore walked no more openly amõge the iewes : butt went his waye thence vnto a countre ny to a wildernes into a cite called effraym / and there haunted with his diſciples.
[…]That yonder in that faithfull wilderneſſe / Huge monſters haunt,and many dangers dwell;[…]

glosses: To accustom; habituate; make accustomed to.

examples.text: […]haunte thi silf to pite [or pitee].

glosses: To practise; to devote oneself to.

examples.text: Leave honest pleasure, and haunt no good pastime.

glosses: To persist in staying or visiting.

examples.text: I haue charg’d thee not to haunt about my doores:[…]

glosses: A place at which one is regularly found; a habitation or hangout.

examples.text: The shopping mall is a popular haunt of the local teenagers in this town.
I went back the town I used to live and visited all my old haunts.

It is a great rock or cliff on the loneliest part of the mountains, and, … is known by the name of the Garden Rock. Near the foot of it is a small lake, the haunt of the solitary bittern, with water-snakes basking in the sun on the leaves of the pond-lilies which lie on the surface.
Both Jack and Fletcher had graduated the year before, but still took an interest in their old haunts, and patronized the fellows who were not yet through.
Wyoming has been a favorite haunt of paleontologists for the past century ever since westering pioneers reported that many vertebrate fossils were almost lying on the ground.
It shall be the haunt of jackals, an abode for ostriches.

glosses: A ghost.
A lair or feeding place of animals.

examples.text: The lofty mountains roſe faint to the ſight and loſt their foreheads in the diſtant ſkies: the little hills, cloathed in darker green and ſkirted with embroidered vales, diſcovered the ſecret haunts of kids and bounding roes.

glosses: Fréquenter quelqu’un que l’on suppose de mauvaise influence ou sur lequel on exerce une mauvaise influence.

examples.text: Autrefois, quand j’étais « cavé », comme dit Tacherot, je hantais de bons bougres qui rêvaient de reprise individuelle. Ça leur coûtait cher.

glosses: Fréquenter quelque lieu mal famé ou sur lequel on exerce une mauvaise influence.

examples.text: Pourtant, d’autres chasseurs hantent ces rivages, avec des intentions moins ludiques : des liches amies, des sérioles ambrées, des tassergals aux dents pointues errent dans la frange côtière, à la poursuite des mulets et orphies.
Je suis un petit V.R.P. Avec mes modestes semblables, je hante de modestes hôtels incroyables de cambrousse, à Ciron, à Scoury, à Migné et j'en passe !
Da Achour hante un taudis au bout d’un chemin flanqué d’une haie en disgrâce et d’une paire de chiens tellement durs à la détente qu’on les supposerait constipés.

glosses: Revenir de l’autre monde, en parlant des esprits.

examples.text: Longtemps encore, la jeune génération du village de Werst croira que les esprits de l’autre monde hantent les ruines du château des Carpathes.

glosses: Remplir, occuper de manière tenace la mémoire ou la pensée de quelqu’un.

examples.text: Il n'en fallut pas davantage pour que les réminiscences qui hantaient sa cervelle prissent subitement un corps.

Maintenant, n’allait-elle pas être hantée par ces mots, qu’elle pouvait interpréter de dix manières ?
